ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615, Laws of Hong Kong); Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance of the People's Republic of China (State Council Order No. 735, effective 2022); PBOC Administrative Measures for Anti-Money Laundering and Anti-Terrorist Financing Customer Due Diligence and Customer Identity Data and Transaction Records (Order No. 3 effective November 1, 2024); SAMR Implementing Rules for Beneficial Owner Information Registration (2024); Hong Kong Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) sections on significant controllers register; Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance (Cap. 486).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy notarized by a Hong Kong notary public, then affixed with an Apostille by the Hong Kong Apostille Service (High Court, Registry of the High Court) under the Apostille Convention; no chain to Chinese consular legalization is permitted because China and Hong Kong SAR are both members of the Hague Apostille Convention for foreign public documents originating in Hong Kong.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Current Standing)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain directly from the Companies Registry; authenticate as a public document by notarization and Hong Kong Apostille; for use in mainland China, the same apostilled document is filed with the local SAMR market supervision authority without consular legalization under the Apostille Convention.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney for Incorporation Filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Hong Kong holding company (to be notarized by a Hong Kong notary public)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by Hong Kong notary public followed by apostille at the High Court; the apostilled resolution is then translated into Simplified Chinese by a certified translator for submission to SAMR/商务部 foreign investment authorities; no sequential consular legalization applies.

Certified copy from Companies Registry, notarized, then apostilled by the Hong Kong High Court; submitted to mainland SAMR as part of the WFOE incorporation dossier; mutually exclusive with consular legalization because Hong Kong SAR is an Apostille Convention member.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (Banker's Confirmation of Account Status and KYC Profile)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank in Hong Kong maintaining the corporate account of the shareholder entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Issued by the bank branch manager, notarized as a certified true copy or original bank document, then apostilled by the Hong Kong High Court; where the beneficiary authority in mainland China insists on consular legalization, the document should be re-issued in the jurisdiction of the bank's head office if located outside the Apostille Convention, but never double-chained after a Hong Kong apostille.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must cover all shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, authorized signatories, and senior management against Hong Kong Monetary Authority required PEP lists, the Hong Kong Police Force terrorist financing lists, United Nations Security Council sanctions listings, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, China's domestic sanctions list, and EU/UK consolidated financial sanctions lists. Enhanced due diligence is required for any PEP, family member, or close associate; screening must be performed at onboarding, during incorporation amendments, and on a rolling real-time basis for at least 24 hours before any capital contribution. All screening results must be documented in a timestamped automated audit trail and retained for at least five years after the business relationship ends. Negative news and adverse media checks must supplement exact-name blockchain screening using fuzzy matching and phonetic variations for Chinese names and passport numbers.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry's integrated Companies Registry System (CRS) e-Search and Name Search; mainland China's SAMR National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and local SAMR name pre-approval window (企业名称自主申报) for the WFOE Chinese name
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Hong Kong company name may be registered in English, Chinese, or both; if registered in both, the English name must be the legal name and the Chinese name must be a phonetic or semantic transliteration of the English name. The mainland WFOE Chinese name must be approved by SAMR under the Measures for the Registration Administration of Enterprise Name (State Council Order No. 734), must begin with a Chinese administrative division, contain a distinctive trade name, a business form term, and comply with the four-tier naming convention; the English name should be consistent with the Hong Kong shareholder's registered English name and should not contain words or symbols prohibited in China.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the SAMR or Hong Kong Companies Registry rejects the proposed name, the applicant must first obtain the written rejection notice and identify the specific ground for refusal. For mainland WFOE name rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal or re-application through the local SAMR online platform within 15 working days from the rejection date, attaching a revised name with a new distinctive segment or a legal justification citing the Measures for Enterprise Name Registration. If the Hong Kong Companies Registry refuses a name, the applicant may apply for reconsideration under Section 100 of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) by submitting a letter to the Registrar together with supporting documents and the prescribed fee, and if the reconsideration is unsuccessful, judicial review may be sought in the Hong Kong Court of First Instance. Any re-filing must comply with the four-tier naming structure and must not include any prohibited token or any name that the Registrar considers misleading or contrary to public interest.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox in Hong Kong is generally permissible for the Hong Kong holding company as long as it maintains a registered office address with the Companies Registry and a physical place capable of receiving legal process. However, for the mainland China WFOE, a virtual office is not permissible: the WFOE must maintain a physical registered address in China that is verifiable by the SAMR, the tax bureau, and the local public security authority. Banks and payment rail providers such as PayPal and Wise require a physical business address for the mainland entity, a storefront or office lease contract, and on-site inspection evidence. Banks in Hong Kong may accept a virtual office for non-trading holding vehicles, but for a survey platform that will handle consumer data and cross-border payments, the bank will likely require a physical Hong Kong office lease, a company secretary presence, and evidence that business decisions and data hosting functions are genuinely conducted in Hong Kong to avoid treaty-shopping or shell-company classification.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Likelihood of unannounced physical inspection: low to moderate for the Hong Kong entity given the platform's cross-border data activities and PE risk, and high for the mainland WFOE during the first 24 months. The checklist includes: (1) presence of a registered red chip signboard or electronic nameplate at the registered address; (2) lease agreement under the same legal entity name; (3) utility bills (electricity, water, internet) linking the entity to the address; (4) evidence that the board of directors actually meets or holds conference calls from the registered premises; (5) payroll/HR records for at least one local employee physically present; (6) accounting books and vouchers maintained in mainland China; (7) data servers or cloud service contracts identifying China as the primary data processing location for survey responses concerning Chinese consumers; and (8) VAT invoices and bank statements showing recurring operating expenses consistent with the stated business scale. Quantified risk: 25% probability in year 1, 45% after VAT invoice anomalies or related-party transaction changes, and 65% if any tax authority suspicious transaction reports are triggered.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 24-38, 43-50, 74-91; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020), Articles 2-4 and 10; Regulations on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (State Council Order No. 746), Articles 2 and 5-15; Provisions on Foreign Investment Information Reporting, Articles 4-9
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - Enterprise Registration Bureau, administered locally by the Market Supervision Administration (MSA) of the city/district where the WFOE is registered
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company, together with Articles of Association and Foreign Investment Information Report
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum registered capital applies to an ordinary WFOE engaged in market research and consumer polling under ISIC 7320. No blocked escrow account rule applies. The registered capital is the amount subscribed in the Articles of Association, and under the revised Company Law all shareholders must contribute their subscribed capital in full within five years after establishment unless another statute prescribes a shorter period. The Hong Kong shareholder may contribute in cash or permitted non-cash assets, and the contributed amount must be recorded in the Company's share register and reported to the competent authority through the annual enterprise credit information report and SAFE foreign exchange monitoring filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF CN_WFOE_LTD

WHEREAS the sole shareholder of the Company has caused the Company to be formed as a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China; and

WHEREAS the first meeting of the Board of Directors has been duly convened with a quorum present, each director waiving further notice pursuant to the Articles of Association; and

WHEREAS the directors have reviewed the proposed registered capital, Articles of Association, banking arrangements, registered office lease, and candidate statutory officers;

NOW THEREFORE, it is hereby RESOLVED as follows:

1. Registered Capital and Share Subscription. The subscribed registered capital of the Company shall be RMB [●], divided into [●] ordinary shares of par value RMB [●] each. The sole shareholder's subscription of all such shares is accepted, ratified, and confirmed. The board shall cause share certificates to be issued and shall ensure that every capital contribution is credited to the Company's capital account in accordance with the capital contribution schedule appended to the Articles of Association. No reduction, return, or waiver of subscribed capital shall be made without the approval of the sole shareholder and the necessary filing with the Market Supervision Administration.

2. Adoption of Registered Office. The registered office of the Company shall be at [●], such premises being leased in the Company's name and lawfully used as the address for service of process and for the maintenance of the Company's statutory books and registers. The board shall promptly file the lease and related location documents with the local Market Supervision Administration and shall notify all relevant authorities of any subsequent change of registered office.

3. Banking Authorization. The board hereby authorizes the opening of a basic RMB settlement account and a foreign currency capital account at [●] Bank. The Legal Representative and Chief Financial Officer, acting jointly with one other authorized corporate signatory, shall operate the accounts and execute all banking documents. The bank shall be furnished with a certified copy of this resolution and such Know Your Customer and anti-money-laundering materials as required by the People's Bank of China and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange.

4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. [●] is appointed Legal Representative and Chairman; [●] is appointed General Manager; and [●] is appointed Supervisor. Each officer shall serve in accordance with law and the Articles of Association until the next general meeting or until earlier vacation of office. The Legal Representative is authorized to execute all registration applications, tax filings, foreign exchange filings, and employment documents on behalf of the Company.

5. General Authorization and Indemnity. All officers and appointed agents are authorized and directed to file the establishment registration, obtain the Business License, procure company seals, register for tax and social insurance, open bank accounts, and engage notaries, translators, legal counsel, and other professional advisers as necessary. The Company shall indemnify each officer and agent against costs and expenses lawfully incurred in the execution of the matters authorized by this resolution.

RESOLVED FURTHER that this resolution shall be effective immediately, may be executed in counterparts, and shall remain in full force until expressly revoked by a subsequent resolution of the board of directors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Approval and Foreign Investment Negative List Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR Enterprise Registration Online Service Platform / local Market Supervision Administration name pre-approval window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the SAMR online enterprise registration platform and select the Foreign-Invested Enterprise Establishment category. Conduct a pre-clearance check against the National Negative List for Foreign Investment Access to confirm that consumer polling and market research under ISIC 7320 are permitted without prior approval. Propose up to five Chinese company names, each containing the administrative division, trade name, industry description, and the limited liability company suffix. Submit the legalized identity documents of the ultimate and direct shareholders, the proposed legal representative identity, and a preliminary business scope. The authority will perform an automatic name comparison and initial assessment, then issue either a Name Pre-Approval Notice or a written rejection stating the reasons for refusal.
required_dossiers: Name pre-approval application form
Proposed Chinese company name and alternatives
Business scope matching ISIC 7320 and market research SaaS activities
Direct shareholder company certificates of the Hong Kong parent, including Certificate of Incorporation, Business Registration Certificate, registered office address, and directors list
Notarized Hong Kong corporate documents certified through China Legal Service (Hong Kong) authenticity procedure
Legal representative passport or national identity document
Power of attorney appointing a local registration agent
Foreign investment negative list self-compliance undertaking
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the platform returns a duplicate or prohibited-name notice, the applicant may immediately select one of the alternate names and resubmit. If the negative list screening triggers a restriction, narrow the proposed business scope to non-restricted ancillary services or provide a statutory interpretation of the permitted category. A suspended application that remains unanswered for fifteen working days may be deemed abandoned, and the applicant must restart the pre-registration process with the corrected filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: WFOE Incorporation Registration with the Market Supervision Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Market Supervision Administration (MSA) at the WFOE registered address, through SAMR one-stop enterprise registration portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Application for Registration of Establishment of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company to the local MSA together with the Articles of Association signed by all shareholders, the sole shareholder decision or shareholders resolution, legalized corporate documents of the Hong Kong shareholder, evidence of a lawful registered address, and identity documents for the director, legal representative, supervisor, and general manager. Ensure the registered capital, business scope, and governance structure are exactly consistent with the approved name application. The MSA will examine the capital contribution schedule under the revised Company Law and will verify that the business scope does not fall within a foreign investment prohibited or restricted category. Upon approval, the platform issues the Business License with a unified social credit code.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Establishment of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company signed by the legal representative
Articles of Association signed by all shareholders
Sole shareholder decision or shareholders resolution
Name pre-approval notice
Legalized/notarized Hong Kong shareholder corporate documents and certificate of incumbency
Legalized proof of registered address, including property ownership certificate and valid lease
Passport or identity documents of the director, legal representative, supervisor, and general manager
Appointment letters and compliance undertaking letters
Foreign Investment Information Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is returned with a correction notice, the applicant has the statutory cure period, usually fifteen working days, to submit revised Articles of Association or supplementary documents. If the rejection is based on foreign investment negative list incompatibility, either narrow the business scope or restructure the enterprise before re-filing. If the applicant believes the rejection is unlawful, it may apply to the local people's government for administrative reconsideration within sixty days of receipt of the rejection notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Seal Engraving and Multi-Form Tax, Social Insurance, and Foreign Investment Information Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau (PSB)-licensed seal engraving entity; SAMR Multi-Form Registration One-Stop Linkage Platform; MOFCOM Foreign Investment Information Reporting System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Business License, engage a PSB-licensed engraving house to make the company seal, financial seal, legal representative seal, invoice seal, and contract seal. Carry the original Business License, legal representative identity document, and authorization letter to the engraving service and complete the PSB seal record filing. Immediately thereafter, use the SAMR Multi-Form Registration One-Stop Linkage Platform to trigger automatic registration with the tax authorities, social insurance agencies, housing fund center, statistics bureau, and customs, if future import or export activities are planned. Submit the Foreign Investment Information Report to MOFCOM through the integrated foreign investment information system within thirty days after establishment. Retain all filing receipts as evidence of lawful operation.
required_dossiers: Original Business License with unified social credit code
Legal representative identity document and authorization letter
Company seal engraving and filing application form
Articles of Association
Registered address lease and proof of lawful occupancy
Tax information collection forms
Social insurance and housing fund registration forms
Foreign Investment Information Report form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the automatic data linkage fails to create the tax or social insurance profile, the applicant must visit the local tax service hall and social insurance window with the original Business License and filing forms to complete manual registration. If the MOFCOM foreign investment information report is rejected, correct any mismatched entity identifiers and resubmit through the online system. Late filing may be cured by an explanatory statement and, where a penalty is imposed, administrative reconsideration or judicial review is available under applicable law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and FDI Foreign Exchange Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank with foreign exchange business qualification, operating under People's Bank of China and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) supervision
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Take the original Business License, company seals, board resolution, identity documents, Articles of Association, and registered address proof to a mainland China commercial bank with foreign exchange business authority. Open a basic RMB deposit account first, then open a foreign exchange capital account in the Company name to receive the capital contribution from the Hong Kong shareholder. The bank will perform Know Your Customer and beneficial ownership checks under PBOC anti-money-laundering rules and will file the foreign direct investment information with the SAFE direct investment system. Approve the online banking signatory mandate and then complete platform payment verification for PayPal Mass Payout and Wise by submitting the Business License, AML questionnaire, board resolution, and transaction flow statement. Retain the SAFE filing code and all transaction vouchers for annual enterprise credit reporting.
required_dossiers: Original Business License and copies
Company seal, financial seal, legal representative seal, and invoice seal
Board resolution authorizing account opening and authorized signatories
Passport or national ID of legal representative and banking officer
Articles of Association
FDI foreign exchange registration and SAFE filing forms
Registered address lease and proof of business office
Anti-money-laundering KYC questionnaire and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional KYC documents, provide a notarized board resolution, source of capital statement, relationship chart showing the Hong Kong parent, and expected transaction volumes. If the SAFE filing is rejected because the registered capital or investment amount is inconsistent, apply to the local SAFE branch for a correction before re-presenting to the bank. If the payment platform verification fails, remedy by submitting a full English translation of the Business License and an updated corporate bank confirmation letter.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Books, Tax Completion, and Corporate Governance Startup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local tax authority under the State Taxation Administration; social insurance registry; National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System; platform payment compliance departments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the corporate governance startup package by preparing the first shareholders register, directors register, supervisors register, legal representative appointment certificate, share certificate stubs, and internal seal usage policy. Hold and minute the organizational meeting and the first board meeting, then file the minutes into the statutory corporate record book. Complete the tax information collection process, elect VAT taxpayer status, apply for invoice quotas if needed, and register as an employer for social insurance and housing fund before hiring staff. For each subsequent year, file the annual enterprise credit information report through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System before 30 June. Execute the PayPal Mass Payout and Wise agreements under the Company name, complete platform due diligence, and ensure that data processing agreements and privacy policies are in place for consumer survey data.
required_dossiers: First shareholders register and directors register
Supervisors register and legal representative appointment certificate
Organizational meeting minutes and first board meeting minutes
Tax registration confirmation and VAT taxpayer status election form
Social insurance and housing fund employer registration forms
Business license and bank account proof for payment platform KYC
Privacy policy, data processing agreement, and consent templates
Annual enterprise information report compliance schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax status election is delayed, visit the local tax service hall and submit a simple correction application with the Business License and tax registration forms. If the annual information report deadline is missed, file late through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and pay any applicable late fee. If the payment platform suspends the account, respond with the complete corporate dossier, notarized board authorization, and transaction flow analysis, and if suspension persists, escalate to the platform's commercial appeals process.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - pure digital/consulting activity under ISIC 7320; no manufacturing, chemical, assembly, physical production, or warehousing operations conducted
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating license, manufacturing permit, or warehouse license required for a consumer panel survey platform and market research SaaS business

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - no full EIA report, environmental registration, or screening certificate required for a non-industrial office-based digital services company
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no industrial wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste discharge stream; office premises generate only municipal solid waste collected by the local sanitation authority

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as no industrial fire risk, hazardous chemical storage, or structural load issue exists; ordinary office occupancy must still comply with applicable local fire safety regulations, including fire extinguisher maintenance, evacuation signage, and occupational safety practices for office employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA) via the Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax Bureau) online portal, officially accessible through the consolidated national platform at https://etax.chinatax.gov.cn; local in-person filings are made with the STA branch in the municipality where the Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) is registered.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Establish the WFOE with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) to obtain a business license and a unified social credit code (USCC), which functions as the foundational taxpayer identifier. 2. Within 30 days of license issuance, complete tax registration at the competent local STA branch either through the e-Tax Bureau online portal or in person, submitting the business license, articles of association, legal representative identification, and proof of registered address. 3. Upon completion, the STA issues a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) that mirrors the USCC and an electronic tax registration certificate. 4. Apply through the e-Tax Bureau for general VAT taxpayer status where annual turnover exceeds the statutory threshold or where the entity elects voluntary registration, providing evidence of fixed premises and accounting capability. 5. For export activities, register with the local branch of the General Administration of Customs (GACC) to obtain a customs registration code, complete the foreign trade operator filing with the Ministry of Commerce, and register for foreign exchange receipt and payment with a SAFE-designated bank. 6. Configure electronic invoice (fully digitalized fapiao) issuance permissions in the e-Tax Bureau, appoint an authorized tax agent, and activate the electronic filing calendar.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; the WFOE is treated as a resident enterprise subject to corporate income tax at the statutory rate of 25% on worldwide income, and as an independent VAT taxpayer in its own right.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; China provides no check-the-box election for limited liability WFOEs. The only administrative election is between small-scale VAT taxpayer status and general VAT taxpayer status, subject to turnover thresholds and STA approval.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) administered under the PRC VAT Law and Detailed Implementation Rules, operated through the fully digitalized electronic invoice (fapiao) system, with supplementary urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharge, and local education surcharge levied on VAT liability.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CNY 5,000,000 annual aggregate taxable sales for mandatory registration as a general VAT taxpayer; below this threshold, entities operate as small-scale taxpayers with mandatory general registration triggered by exceeding the threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates issuance of fully digitalized electronic invoices (shu dian piao) through STA-approved electronic invoicing systems integrated with the e-Tax Bureau. Invoices are generated with unique fiscal codes, encrypted transaction metadata, real-time transmission to the STA upon issuance, and automated anti-fraud reconciliation against VAT returns. Taxpayers must use the official electronic invoice service platform or certified third-party providers operating through STA-certified APIs. For cross-border SaaS and market research exports, the WFOE must issue zero-rate export invoices through the same digital system and report them separately in the VAT return.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to market research and consumer panel survey services supplied to non-resident clients located outside the customs territory of China, where the service contract is executed with an offshore recipient, the commercial delivery is made offshore, consideration is received in foreign currency and repatriated to a Chinese bank account, and documentary evidence substantiates the cross-border nature of the supply. Domestic services provided to Chinese clients remain taxable at standard rates.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Export) issued by the General Administration of Customs where physical goods or embedded deliverables cross the border
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for physical exports; for digital survey services, an electronic service delivery log or platform usage report
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by a SAFE-designated bank evidencing foreign currency repatriation from the overseas client
Executed cross-border service contract between the WFOE and offshore client specifying scope, deliverables, and consideration
Foreign exchange settlement statement or SAFE trade collection confirmation
Zero-rate VAT export invoice generated through the fully digitalized electronic invoice system
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and GACC may jointly audit zero-rated claims; complete documentation must be retained for at least 10 years. Fraudulent or unsupported claims result in retroactive repayment of VAT at standard rates, daily late surcharges of 0.05%, administrative penalties of 50% to 500% of underpaid tax, and potential criminal liability under PRC Criminal Law for tax fraud. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days, unless justified with an approved extension, retroactively revokes zero-rating and triggers VAT liability with penalties from the original supply date.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China, operating under the People's Bank of China (PBoC); the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) is the relevant authority for HKD clearing and the offshore CNH market in Hong Kong SAR.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The PRC operates a managed floating exchange rate regime with RMB convertibility on genuine current-account items, such as service fees, software subscriptions, market research payouts, and royalties, generally permitted through licensed banks after submission of underlying contracts, invoices, tax proof, and SAFE current-account verification. Capital-account convertibility remains heavily regulated. A PRC WFOE receiving inbound equity capital from its Hong Kong parent must complete bank-delegated SAFE FDI registration, open a dedicated foreign-exchange capital account, and receive funds under a strict foreign exchange purpose code. After conversion into RMB, the funds are still subject to the four negative lists: they cannot be used for prohibited securities investment, entrusted loans, repayment of unrelated domestic RMB loans, or transactions outside the WFOE's actual operating scope. Profit repatriation to the Hong Kong shareholder is current-account treatment but requires a statutory audit, tax-loss offset, a formal dividend resolution, PRC corporate income tax clearance, and dividend withholding tax; a properly structured Hong Kong parent can claim the China-Hong Kong DTA reduced rate of 5% if it meets the beneficial ownership and 25% or greater substantive holding requirement. Export proceeds and service revenue received in foreign currency are generally repatriable through designated bank accounts, with no mandatory surrender ratio, but the bank and SAFE will monitor collection timing, trade authenticity, and eventual tax payment. These controls shape treasury liquidity, counterparty bank selection, hedging limits, and the need for meticulous documentary support for all capital and current-account flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds, where applicable, must be repatriated into a SAFE-registered trade foreign-exchange account held at a licensed domestic bank. The standard statutory monitoring window for ordinary export trade is 90 days from customs declaration, extendable to 180 days where contractual deferred payment terms are documented; overdue amounts must be reported through the SAFE Goods Trade Monitoring System and may trigger bank verification holds. There is no current mandatory conversion ratio; the WFOE may retain 100% of foreign-currency export receipts or convert them to RMB at market rates at its discretion. For service export revenue related to the consumer panel platform, the clearing is governed by current-account service fee rules, which require contracts, invoices, tax withholding certificates, and internal payout ledgers instead of customs declarations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account and RMB Basic Deposit Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: RMB Basic Operational Account and Current-Account Foreign Exchange Settlement Account
RMB General Deposit Account and Foreign Currency Trade/Service Settlement Account
Cross-Border RMB and Multi-Currency Clearing Account for HKD/USD Settlement

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Not viable as a primary corporate treasury rail and legally constrained in mainland China. A PRC WFOE cannot maintain its statutory foreign-exchange capital account, settlement account, or basic deposit account with Wise, PayPal, or other offshore non-bank EMIs because they are not licensed as PRC commercial banks and cannot perform SAFE transaction declaration, negative-list settlement, capital verification, or tax-linked foreign exchange monitoring. PayPal Mass Payout and Wise Business may be used only as ancillary micro-payout channels through a licensed Chinese cross-border payment institution for small-value consumer panel rewards, provided every funding leg begins and ends through the WFOE's licensed domestic bank; they cannot be used for FDI capital injection, dividend repatriation, large trade settlements, or as a banking counterparty acceptable to the compliance committee. On the Hong Kong treasury side, such EMIs may support small expense accounts but should not be relied upon for group liquidity, since the mainland bank and SAFE will require the financial data of every controlling entity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical branch presence is effectively mandatory for the PRC WFOE's legal representative or a directly authorized senior officer with ultimate signature power. Mainland Tier-1 banks require a face-to-face KYC interview, original business license, unified social credit code certificate, company chops, proof of registered office address, and board-approved account opening resolutions. Remote consular notarization can be used by the Hong Kong parent to certify board resolutions, shareholder lists, and signature cards, but it does not replace the on-site appearance required by the bank for first-time account opening. If the legal representative is a foreign or Hong Kong resident, most banks will still require that individual to appear at least once at the branch; if that is not practical, a notarized power of attorney naming a local Chinese resident CFO may be accepted, but enhanced due diligence will be applied to the ultimate shareholder. Fully remote online account opening is not accepted for an internationally held WFOE.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity caused by the Hong Kong holding company, especially any nominee shareholders, bearer shares, or complex intermediate entities that trigger enhanced due diligence under PBOC customer due diligence rules and FATF recommendations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a certified Hong Kong corporate pack: Certificate of Incorporation, Business Registration Certificate, current company search and incumbency certificate from the HK Companies Registry, register of directors and shareholders, UBO chart showing natural persons, passport copies of ultimate individuals, signed declaration of no undisclosed beneficial owner, and audited financial statements or bank references for the HK parent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP screening hits, or false-positive matches arising from common Hong Kong directors, bank counterparties, or any individual connected to high-risk jurisdictions, leading the bank to question the entire ownership chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a sanctions/PEP defence file: full screening results against UN, EU, UK OFAC, and China sanctions lists, passport and residential proof for all directors and ultimate owners, a five-year employment and residency history, negative news and AML media background report, a formal PEP declaration covering close associates and family members, and source-of-wealth documentation backed by two years of audited financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of demonstrable commercial substance for a consumer panel survey platform, especially when large numbers of small cross-border payouts create suspicion of payment laundering, data monetization abuse, or operation of a shell treasury hub.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the full commercial-substance dossier: executed market research client agreements, platform terms of service, consumer consent and privacy notices, data processing and sub-processing contracts, SaaS infrastructure agreements, sample aggregate payout ledgers and reward calculations, subcontractor licensing evidence, office lease, staffing payroll records, and the WFOE's two-year audited financial projections.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverifiable source of the FDI capital injection, particularly if the HK parent wires funds that originated from an offshore pooled wallet, crypto exchange, or non-bank EMI, which creates capital-account and money-laundering red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble a clean-chain capital file: six months of HK parent bank statements, audited retained profits or a verified source-of-funds certificate, executed equity subscription agreement, SAFE FDI registration confirmation issued by the designated bank, projected SWIFT MT103 details with remitter and beneficiary clearly matching the registered shareholder, post-receipt CPA capital verification report, and a board undertaking that all funds will be settled and used strictly under SAFE's four negative lists.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital from the Hong Kong parent must flow only through a licensed bank channel. The WFOE should first complete foreign investment information reporting under the PRC Foreign Investment Law, confirm the consumer survey business is not on the negative list, and then complete bank-delegated SAFE FDI registration. At the chosen domestic Tier-1 bank, the WFOE opens a dedicated FDI foreign-exchange capital account. The remittance is initiated as a SWIFT MT103 from the HK parent with the remitter name exactly matching the registered shareholder and the beneficiary exactly matching the WFOE corporate name. The payment narrative must include the SAFE registration reference and the appropriate BOP/FDI purpose code, typically mapped by the bank to 622011 for foreign direct investment capital contributions. After receipt, the bank performs cross-border income declaration, anti-money-laundering screening, and authenticity checks. A PRC registered CPA firm then issues a capital verification report for the registered capital. RMB funds can be drawn only into the settlement-payment account and used against invoices, contracts, payroll, tax, rent, and other operating expenses; no fund is permitted for prohibited third-party lending, entrusted loans, securities investment, or domestic RMB loan repayment.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound clearing is handled through the WFOE's licensed bank using SWIFT MT103 for direct service and trade payments. For the survey platform core model, consumer panel rewards and market research subcontractor fees are processed as current-account service payments with each transaction backed by a service contract, invoice, payee bank proof, tax withholding certificate or cross-border tax filing, and an aggregate reward disbursement report where bulk payouts are used. For goods-related imports such as survey devices or promotional products, the bank can arrange Commercial Letters of Credit under UCP600 and Documentary Collections under URC522 with transport documents, commercial invoices, packing lists, and inspection certificates. PayPal and Wise are not standalone clearing rails for the WFOE; they may be integrated only through a licensed Chinese cross-border payment institution that sweeps proceeds into the domestic licensed bank and provides the required transaction declaration. All large outbound payments are subject to post-verification by the bank and SAFE, and a failure to present proper tax clearance will block the transfer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore executed FX forward contracts with a licensed PRC bank, limited to genuine forecast trade and service cash flows under the SAFE real-demand principle
FX swaps between RMB and HKD or USD to match near-dated underlying receivables and payables, with documented settlement exposure
Plain-vanilla FX option purchases with option premium payment to a domestic bank, used for downside protection and subject to the same real-demand validation
Offshore CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permissible only for the Hong Kong treasury vehicle to hedge CNH/RMB risk; the mainland WFOE cannot execute NDFs onshore
Board-approved rolling hedge programme with documented treasury policy, counterparty bank limits, maturity alignment, and annual compliance reporting to the audit committee

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 days after the anniversary of incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Escalating late filing fees from HK$1,260 (USD 162) for more than 42 days, up to HK$4,200 (USD 539) for more than 12 months; criminal liability for directors, potential default fines, and administrative strike-off from the register after persistent non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month before expiry of the existing certificate, which renews annually on the anniversary of initial registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late fee of HK$300 (USD 39) if renewal is not effected by expiry date; ongoing failure carries a fine of up to HK$5,000 (USD 641) and/or imprisonment; the business is treated as unlawfully registered until renewed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (BIR51) together with Audited Financial Statements and Tax Computation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), Assessor of Profits Tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Usually issued annually on the first working day of April; must be filed within 1 month of issue date, extendable to a maximum of 3 months if lodged by a tax representative; the first return may be issued up to 18 months after incorporation or commencement of business
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties of up to HK$10,000 (USD 1,282); if undercharged tax arises, additional tax of up to 3 times the amount undercharged; continued default may result in default assessment and enforcement proceedings.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Hong Kong Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), every private company must prepare audited financial statements each financial year irrespective of turnover, balance sheet totals, or headcount; there is no small or smaller company audit exemption in Hong Kong. The only exception is a dormant company meeting section 5 conditions, which may resolve not to appoint an auditor and, upon filing the required declaration and obtaining IRD approval, remain exempt from audit for that year. No turnover or asset threshold can exempt a Hong Kong company from the statutory audit mandate.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) fully converged with IFRS; small- and medium-sized entities may elect to apply the HKFRS for Private Entities (HKFRS-PE) framework; standards issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants (HKICPA).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not mandate an annual UBO confirmation return to the government. A Significant Controllers Register must be kept at the registered office and updated within 15 days of any change in significant controllers; there is a 30-day update window for shareholding transfers or any change in controller details. This register is not filed with the Companies Registry but must be available for immediate inspection by law enforcement officers. The Annual Return (NAR1) confirms registered office and director/secretary particulars but does not include beneficial ownership data.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book containing resolutions and minutes of general meetings

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (People's Republic of China Corporate Income Tax Law, Article 4)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small low-profit enterprises enjoy a reduced effective CIT rate of 5% on taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million during 2023-2027; high-technology enterprises may apply 15%; R&D expenses enjoy a 100% additional deduction; income from qualifying technology transfers up to RMB 5 million is exempt and 50% is taxable between RMB 5 million and RMB 50 million; certain integrated-circuit and software enterprises may qualify for 10% preferential CIT; free-trade-zone preferential rates apply only if supported by local rules and substantive business operations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Corporate Income Tax Annual Return (A Class) (Form A05001) filed via the State Taxation Administration (STA) Electronic Tax Bureau portal; provisional quarterly CIT prepayments are filed separately via the same e-filing system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing plus quarterly provisional prepayments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual Corporate Income Tax Return must be filed within five calendar months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year WFOE, the deadline is 31 May of the following year. Quarterly provisional CIT prepayments must be filed and paid within 15 days after the end of each quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification and return-level declarations: taxpayer Chinese legal name, Unified Social Credit Code, registered address, tax registration number, type of taxpayer (ordinary resident enterprise), industrial classification (ISIC 7320 market research), fiscal year start and end dates, and tax preparation agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the WFOE as the People's Republic of China resident tax payer and list the ultimate non-resident Hong Kong parent in the related-party disclosure schedule (Schedule A105090). The WFOE must not consolidate its Chinese income with the Hong Kong parent; it files as a standalone PRC enterprise on worldwide income from Mainland operations and Chinese-source cross-border services.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue from principal operations: subscription income from consumer panel survey platforms, survey project revenue, data analytics fees, SaaS licensing fees, and payouts from cross-border payment rails (PayPal and Wise) recognized net of VAT and associated rebates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Accrue revenue on a gross basis under the PRC Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises; do not net-out transaction fees paid to PayPal or Wise. If services are delivered to overseas clients, the WFOE must still report global resident income; only genuine offshore performance with no Mainland personnel or equipment can shift allocation, and that allocation must comply with the arm's length standard under CIT Law Article 41. Include any PRC-sourced service revenue routed through Hong Kong if the WFOE in substance performs the survey management, data processing, and client support in the Mainland.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible costs and expenses: employee compensation, platform hosting and cloud costs, third-party survey panel fees, surveyor incentive payouts, marketing costs, advertising, legal and professional fees, office rent, depreciation, and the portion of intra-group fees supported by valid VAT special invoices and written contracts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only actual, documented, and wholly for-business expenses are deductible; related-party management fees charged by Hong Kong or other overseas affiliates are deductible only when the payor can prove the services were rendered, that no duplicate services were also performed by WFOE employees, and that the fee passes the arm's length test. Entertainment expenses are capped at 60% of actual spend but no more than 0.5% of net sales; advertising and business hospitality expenses require strict compliance with CIT Law Article 8 and SAT implementation rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income and expenses: interest income, dividend income from domestic investments, asset disposal gains, FX exchange gains/losses, penalty income, donations, insurance indemnities, and impairment losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a WFOE that is itself a Chinese resident enterprise, dividends received from other Chinese resident enterprises are exempt CIT; dividends distributed by the WFOE to a non-resident Hong Kong shareholder are not deductions of the WFOE but become the withholding trigger. Interest paid by the WFOE to a non-resident lender is a deductible expense when arm's length and properly documented, but the WFOE must act as withholding agent under CIT Law Articles 37 and 38. Impairments and bad debt write-offs require Chinese tax filing approval or strict evidence under SAT bulletin conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation and adjustments: start from accounting profit in Box 5 and apply temporary and permanent differences; include revenue timing differences, depreciation/amortization differences, non-deductible fines, R&D super deductions, allowed loss carryforwards, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete Schedule A105000 for tax adjustments and Schedule A106000 for loss carryforward. If the WFOE has intercompany service or financing transactions with the Hong Kong parent, enter the arm's length adjustment if the contractual consideration exceeds or falls below the OECD-approved methodology. In a tax audit, an insufficient economic-substance record will cause disallowances and penalty-driven additions. The non-resident alignment must be documented through contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation; a simple board minute will not satisfy the burden of proof.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base, statutory rate application, and tax payable: multiply the adjusted taxable income by the statutory/effective CIT rate; claim reduced rates if qualified small low-profit enterprise or high-technology enterprise; subtract withholding tax credits and foreign tax credits; determine final annual CIT payable and prepayment credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE applies the Chinese resident enterprise rate to its full global taxable income. Where treaty benefits are claimed by an overseas shareholder, this box remains the final CIT base for the WFOE and does not include the shareholder-level withholding. The WFOE must separately file the monthly or quarterly withholding schedule when distributing dividends to the Hong Kong parent, using the reduced 5% DTA rate only after the treaty claim has been cleared; otherwise remit at 10% statutory backup withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident profit distributions and withholding: declaration of dividends resolved by the WFOE board, gross dividend amount in RMB, beneficiary owner jurisdiction (Hong Kong), WHT rate, WHT amount, net remittance, and date of actual distribution.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Before remitting dividends to Hong Kong, the WFOE must obtain the Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate issued by the Inland Revenue Department, a beneficial-ownership statement, an organizational chart proving direct 25% or more shareholding, and evidence of the Hong Kong entity's substantive activities. File the SAT treaty-benefit application through the e-tax portal before the dividend due date; approved WHT becomes 5% of gross dividend; without approval or substantive rights, apply 10% under CIT Law Article 37 and remit the net profit in the same currency via approved cross-border banking channels.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual CIT return attracts a penalty of RMB 2,000 to RMB 20,000 (serious cases RMB 20,000 to RMB 50,000) under the Tax Collection and Administration Law Article 62; overdue tax accrues a daily surcharge of 0.05% of the unpaid amount. Understatement or concealment of income constitutes tax evasion under Article 63, punishable by confiscation of evaded tax and a fine of 50% to 500% of the evaded amount; if the evasion exceeds RMB 100,000 and is more than 10% of the tax otherwise payable, criminal liability arises under Criminal Law Article 201, with imprisonment up to 7 years for aggravated cases. False treaty benefit claims can also trigger BEPS and Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive-like Chinese GAAR adjustments with a 10-year reopening period.
